title: Split Variable

solutions.title: Two named results instead of one reused variable
solutions.tradeoff: The metered fare and the deposit refund each get their own name and their own line, so a function that used to read as one running number now reads as two - a fair trade for a reader no longer having to track which question the shared variable currently answers.

reviewFocus: Does the loop's accumulator (now meteredFareCents) still answer only 'what does the meter say', or does anything downstream write into it for a second, unrelated purpose?
Is depositRefundCents a const, assigned exactly once? A let there would suggest it still has more than one job.
Does totalDueCents read meteredFareCents and depositRefundCents directly, or does it still route through a shared temp that could reintroduce the smell?
Would you have kept the deposit refund's zero case as a ternary or extracted a named predicate - and does the expression read as one sentence at the call site?
Compare the loop accumulator's let to depositRefundCents's const: does the split make that distinction visible at a glance, or does a reader still have to trace assignments to tell them apart?
